weeks.note: RECOVERY WEEK. Upper/Lower split: two upper sessions (Tue, Fri) so chest and back get 2x frequency at zero cost to running; one lower session (Thu), which is all the race can afford. Only two sessions actually matter: the talk test on a cool morning, and Saturday's descents.

sessions.label: UPPER A (push-emphasis) — bench/press + a row. No leg cost, won't touch tomorrow's test.
TALK TEST 5 km — MORNING, cool, fresh. Step the pace up every 3-5 min, say a sentence aloud, note the HR where it turns from comfortable to 'comfortable but harder'.
LOWER — own day, no running. Strength focus (squat/split squat, single-leg RDL, calf, tib, glute-med). NOT eccentric-emphasised — Saturday is the eccentric day.
Easy run 4 km (talk test) — or the TALK TEST if Wednesday slipped
UPPER B (pull-emphasis) — pull-ups/rows + a press. Second upper session: chest and back both hit 2x this week.
Vertical 25 min (stairs/ramp/incline) — climbing
Controlled stair/ramp descents after the vertical — THE eccentric session. First real descent load.

weeks.note: Barcelona Tue-Fri, then festival at Amsterdamse Bos (Fri evening, Sat, Sun). Down week — the travel timing is ideal; nothing here builds fitness. Benchmark deferred to a cool, recovered morning (Week 6). The long run folds into Sat festival morning. Festival walking covers the volume; do not add load.

sessions.label: Easy 3 km — Barcelona, early AM by feel. Heat inflates HR; ignore pace and HR, run by breath.
Optional vertical — hike Montjuic or Bunkers del Carmel in Barcelona. No benchmark this week; heat and travel would void the data.
Long run 6-7 km — Sat morning from Lelylaan into Amsterdamse Bos, easy by feel; scope the festival grounds. Hydrate hard before the day.

weeks.note: EASY RE-ENTRY — recovering from the festival weekend. No max efforts, no heavy legs, no CP test (moved to Week 6, now a power test on fresh legs). Optional easy 4 km Thu or rest — your call. Run easy by feel, hydrate; only if you feel decent. Getting back to baseline is the whole job this week.

sessions.label: Easy 4-5 km recovery jog — by feel, conversational, ignore pace/HR. Walk it in if you feel rough.
Easy 5-6 km by feel. Optional light pull if you are feeling good.
Easy bike ride instead of the long run — zero impact, aerobic recovery. Keep it chill; save the legs for Tuesday's power test.

weeks.note: First real fitness read of the block — the CP power test, Tuesday on fresh legs (Mon rest before it). Power, not HR: after the sensor audit, power is the channel we trust. This sets your real training zones. HR benchmark is shelved until a chest strap.

weeks.note: RESET WEEK. Two corrections that change everything. (1) You have steep terrain 20-25 MINUTES away - Zuid-Kennemerland dunes by train, faces at 30-45%. I told you the nearest hills were 2.5-3 h; that was wrong. (2) Your plan's vertical is an ORDER OF MAGNITUDE short: 40 min/week is ~400 m against a 2,003 m race. From here everything is measured in time and vertical metres, never kilometres. LOCKED WEEK SHAPE: Sun optional easy ride - MON REST - TUE legs + preconditioning walk ONLY (this is THE eccentric day - keep it focused, no upper) - WED easy run + strides + push - THU vertical + pull - FRI REST - SAT LONG DAY. Eccentric work sits 48 h apart throughout: Tue heavy, Thu moderate, Sat long. That spacing is the constraint - force loss needs 3 days to recover and soreness 4, so 24 h between eccentric sessions compounds damage instead of building tolerance. Cutbacks weeks 10 and 13. CUT ORDER: (1) Sunday ride, (2) Thursday vertical. Never Saturday's long day or Tuesday's legs. HYROX SEEDING STARTS: only via substitution inside Thursday's pull session - erg warm-up, farmers carry, dead hangs. NOT wall balls, sandbag lunges or burpee broad jumps - those are all quad and eccentric load competing directly with the descent block. NOT compromised running - it breaks the 80/20 distribution Madeira needs. The point is to arrive in November with technique and grip already built, so the first two Hyrox weeks are productive instead of remedial.

sessions.label: OPTIONAL easy ride 60-75 min - the day after the long day. Zero impact. THIS IS THE FIRST THING TO CUT when work bites.
Easy run 6 km (talk test) + 6-8 x 20 s strides after (relaxed, full recovery, not a workout)
Push (upper) - after the easy run. Fresh, not on legs you just destroyed.

Legs ONLY, no upper - heavy eccentric. Three quad lifts doing three different jobs: HEAVY BILATERAL trap-bar deadlift 4 x 4-6 at 80-85% 1RM (~72-78 kg), LOADED UNILATERAL Bulgarian split squat 3 x 8/leg with dumbbells, and TEMPO ECCENTRIC step-downs 3 x 8-10/leg with 3-4 s lowering. Then Nordics 3 x 5 and single-leg calf raises. Never to failure. 48-72 h before the long day. On a -15% descent hip drop is 23.7 mm vs 7.6 mm uphill (very large effect), so descending is a frontal-plane hip problem and not only a quad problem - loaded Bulgarians carry that demand, which is why standalone side planks and cable abduction came out. HYROX SLED TECHNIQUE at the end, 8-10 x 12.5 m at 50-65% load (~100 kg), 60-90 s rest. TECHNIQUE ONLY, never to fatigue. Forearms hooked on the posts, 30-45 deg lean, short choppy steps 20-30 cm at 3-4 per second, and never let the sled stop. Sled push is PURELY CONCENTRIC, so it costs your descent block nothing - which is why it is the one Hyrox station you can train now. At 56 kg you need 1.03x bodyweight of horizontal force to break a stationary sled versus 0.81x to keep one rolling, so learning not to stop is worth more to you than to anyone heavier. About 8 minutes.

VERTICAL 45 min - STAIRWELL, your own building or a car park. ~12 x 15 floors, about 540 m. Lift up, WALK DOWN - the descent is the point. Dutch stair pitch is 30-33 deg, inside the optimal climbing range, and Madeira is full of stone staircases. Zero travel, weather-proof.

Pull (upper) - after the vertical session. HYROX SEEDING, all substitutions not additions: (1) WARM UP ON THE SKIERG OR ROWER, 5-8 min, technique only - hinge and drive the first third of the pull, that is where 80% of ski power comes from. Replaces your normal warm-up, costs nothing. (2) SWAP one row variation for a HEAVY FARMERS CARRY, 4 x 40-60 m. Same pulling pattern, direct Hyrox transfer. (3) Finish with DEAD HANGS, 2-3 x max, target 90 s by October. Grip takes 4-6 weeks to change and it is what limits the farmers carry. About 3 minutes total added to the session.
LONG DAY 1:50 time-on-feet, 300 m vert. Dunes if you can get there.

PRECONDITIONING DOWNHILL WALK - 5 minutes, 5.6 kg in the pack, walking DOWN stairs. Lift up, walk down, repeat for 5 min. ~110 m of descent, about 37 flights. One bout cuts strength loss 49%, CK 47%, soreness 66% a week later. Five minutes, in your own building, no travel.

weeks.note: Poles introduced this week. They save little metabolically but cut RPE 14-18% and measurably reduce muscle damage over a climb-and-descent day. Length = 58% of your height = ~93 cm, shorter than a standard fitting. Confirm Ultra X's pole policy.

weeks.note: GUT TRAINING STARTS. Target 60-80 g carb/h by week 14, from 40-50 now, +10 g every two weeks. No drop bags and no crew at Madeira - only ~2 checkpoints, ~10 km apart - so you carry 400-500 g of carbohydrate yourself. Rehearse the weight and the stowage, not just the products. INTENSITY STARTS THIS WEEK. Thursday's vertical becomes intervals - the plan had no hard sessions at all through weeks 7-8, which was a gap. Target distribution is 80-85% easy, 15-20% hard, with the hard work on incline.

weeks.note: TERRAIN WEEKEND #2 - POSBANK AGAIN, not the Ardennes. Roughly EUR 30 of petrol against EUR 200, and twenty reps of a 90-110 m climb is 1,800 m of ascent AND hard-surface descent - close to the whole race. Sustained descending on firm ground is the one thing stairs cannot replicate, and it is what decides your day. POLES: bought 18-20 Sep, so you have had three weeks on them by now. Use them the whole session. They cut RPE 14-18% and measurably reduce muscle damage over a climb-and-descent day - but an inexperienced pole user in a field study actually got SLOWER, so the practice is the point. KIT-CHECK HABIT STARTS HERE: every food item must be labelled with its calorie count, and all disposable packaging must carry your bib number. Tape a strip on your gel flask reading contents and total kcal (e.g. '4x Upfront Gel PRO - 640 kcal'). Do it from this session on, not at registration.

Sled push is PURELY CONCENTRIC, so it costs your descent block nothing - which is why it is the one Hyrox station you can train now. About 8 minutes.

Steady climbing for whatever time is left. Pull (upper) - after the vertical session. HYROX SEEDING, all substitutions not additions: (1) WARM UP ON THE SKIERG OR ROWER, 5-8 min, technique only - hinge and drive the first third of the pull, that is where 80% of ski power comes from. (3) Finish with DEAD HANGS, 2-3 x max, target 90 s by October. Grip takes 4-6 weeks to change and it is what limits the farmers carry. About 3 minutes total added to the session.
LONG DAY 3:20, 1,400 m vert - Posbank, hard-surface descents, full kit, poles, race fuelling. Switch from DIY mix to race gels this week: everything you carry now must be labelled.

weeks.note: PEAK WEEKEND - Sat 17 Oct, 15 days out. This is the overload the taper is built on; the evidence favours peaking 14-15 days out, not five weeks. 3:45-4:00 and 1,600-1,800 m: roughly 60-70% of race duration but 80-90% of race vertical. Vertical specificity is the lever, not duration.

PEAK LONG DAY 3:45-4:00, 1,600-1,800 m vert. Race kit, poles, race fuelling, race shoes. Alternate 20-25 min climbing with 15-20 min flat to rehearse the sawtooth. DESCENT CUE: shorten the step, 185-195 spm. Understriding cut strength loss to -8.8% vs -15.5% at preferred step length - roughly halved. Do NOT coach foot strike: the more anterior the strike, the LARGER the quad torque loss. Let the terrain dictate it.

PRECONDITIONING DOWNHILL WALK - 5 minutes, 5.6 kg in the pack, walking DOWN stairs. Lift up, walk down, repeat for 5 min. ~110 m of descent, about 37 flights. One bout cuts strength loss 49%, CK 47%, soreness 66% a week later. Five minutes, in your own building, no travel.

weeks.note: Taper starts. Volume down 45-55%, intensity and frequency UNCHANGED - that combination is worth 2-3%, about 7-11 minutes on a 6-hour race. NOTHING ECCENTRIC AFTER 21 OCTOBER. Last heavy lower-body work is done.

Push (upper) - after the easy run. Fresh, not on legs you just destroyed.

VERTICAL 40 min - STAIRWELL, your own building or a car park. ~11 x 15 floors, about 495 m. Lift up, WALK DOWN - the descent is the point. Dutch stair pitch is 30-33 deg, inside the optimal climbing range, and Madeira is full of stone staircases. Zero travel, weather-proof.
LAST LONG SESSION 2:00, 600-800 m vert, race kit and shoes, ~20 min of downhill

weeks.note: RACE WEEK. Sunday 1 Nov, Calhau de Sao Jorge to Machico. THE START IS 11:00, NOT DAWN - sunset is 18:17 and civil twilight ends 18:41. A 6:30 finish is daylight; 7:00 is dusk; 7:30 is DARK on exposed cliff paths. YOUR HEADTORCH IS SAFETY KIT, NOT A FORMALITY - carry it charged. The late start also gives you an unhurried fuelling morning: eat properly, this is an advantage. CHECKPOINTS ARE WATER ONLY - the 'water and snacks' line is wrong. Carry 420-490 g of carbohydrate yourself (~13 gels plus mix) across three ~2h10 legs, roughly 2.6 kg of vest. Only ~2 checkpoints, ~10 km apart. KIT: 1.5 L hydration capacity, taped-seam hooded waterproof, emergency blanket, 800 kcal reserve, phone with GPX, spare warm layer, and a BEAKER of at least 15 cl - bottles and flasks are explicitly not accepted. Checks are enforced. CALIBRATION from the 2025 field (n=34): winner 3:02:21, median 5:24:37 (13.0 min/km), last finisher 8:03:43, cut-off 11.5 h. Your target is 6:15-6:45. The 25K is the final 25 km of the 50K route - the organiser gave the SHORT race the STEEPEST ground, 80 m/km against 63.5 for the 50K. PACING - the single strongest result in the literature (n=23,207): in 91% of races, slower finishers overspent in the FIRST segment; after the opening everyone paces the rest alike. The damage is done at the start. Hike every gradient above 15% from the gun. HR: race average 138-150, climb ceiling 155, descents 120-140. Above 160 for two minutes on a climb, walk. Your 17 km run averaged 163 - you cannot hold that for six hours. THE DESCENT IS THE RACE. Racing the first steep descent saves ~10 minutes and costs 17-46 minutes later: 3:1 to 5:1 against, before you count the fall risk. And it will never feel hard - VO2 on descents is only 79% of threshold versus 100% uphill, so your breathing will tell you nothing. That is the trap. Short steps, 185-195 spm, gaze 4-5 m ahead on the second upcoming foothold, walk the stone staircases, zig-zag the wet sections. IN-RACE DIAGNOSTIC: compare climb rate per heartbeat on the second climb against the first. More than 5% worse means you overcooked the descent - concede ten minutes immediately and save the day. FUEL: 60-75 g/h at 2:1 glucose:fructose, drink to thirst, skip the salt capsules (no evidence they prevent hyponatraemia or cramp). Carb load 8-10 g/kg for 36-48 h = 450-560 g. Caffeine ~100 mg at 3 h and 75-100 mg at 4.5 h, 150-200 mg total - do not scale from 70 kg examples. WEATHER: use Santana on the north coast, not Funchal - 18 C max, 110 mm of rain across ~40% of days. Wet basalt and hypothermia are the risks here, not heat. Bib pickup Fri 30 Oct or Sat 31 Oct, 18:00-20:00, Machico Forum. No crew, no pacers, no drop bags.
